MATHEMATICS — MOCK EXAM #5
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which list shows all the factors of 24? (1 mark)
   A. 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24
   B. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 12, 24
   C. 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24
   D. 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12

2. Which is the largest number: 538, 583, 358, 385? (1 mark)
   A. 583
   B. 385
   C. 358
   D. 538

3. Round 128 to the nearest ten. (1 mark)
   A. 140
   B. 130
   C. 100
   D. 120

4. Round 205 to the nearest ten. (1 mark)
   A. 310
   B. 220
   C. 200
   D. 210

5. How many times do you need to regroup when you add 1,234 + 4,321? (1 mark)
   A. 2
   B. 0
   C. 3
   D. 1

6. What is the rule of the pattern 750, 1,000, 1,250, 1,500? (1 mark)
   A. subtract 250
   B. add 750
   C. add 500
   D. add 250

7. Estimate 2,694 + 3,158 by rounding each number to the nearest ten. (1 mark)
   A. 5,952
   B. 5,850
   C. 5,860
   D. 5,840

8. What is the next number in the pattern 9,000, 8,500, 8,000, 7,500, ...? (1 mark)
   A. 7,500
   B. 6,500
   C. 7,000
   D. 8,500

9. Work out 9,250 − 4,875. (1 mark)
   A. 4,375
   B. 5,625
   C. 4,275
   D. 4,385

10. What is 48 × 100? (1 mark)
   A. 480
   B. 4,800
   C. 148
   D. 48,000

11. Dan writes some fractions. Which of these is a proper fraction? (1 mark)
   A. 13/6
   B. 1/2
   C. 8/3
   D. 4 2/3

12. A rectangle is cut into 10 equal parts and 7 of the parts are shaded. What fraction of the rectangle is shaded? (1 mark)
   A. 10/7
   B. 7/10
   C. 7/3
   D. 3/10

13. Why must the parts be equal when we write the fraction 1/3? (1 mark)
   A. The parts can be any size
   B. Only the shaded part must be equal
   C. The whole is cut into three parts of the same size
   D. The numerator must be 3

14. What is 1/4 of 36? (1 mark)
   A. 5
   B. 9
   C. 27
   D. 18

15. Which is the largest number: 0.9, 0.09, 0.85, 0.099? (1 mark)
   A. 0.9
   B. 0.099
   C. 0.09
   D. 0.85

16. In the number 26.91, the digit 2 is in which place? (1 mark)
   A. Ones
   B. Tenths
   C. Hundredths
   D. Tens

17. Which pair are like terms? (1 mark)
   A. 3a and 5a
   B. 3a and 5b
   C. 4 and 4z
   D. 2x and 2y

18. A pencil starts at the 4 cm mark on a ruler and ends at the 12 cm mark. How long is the pencil? (1 mark)
   A. 8 cm
   B. 12 cm
   C. 16 cm
   D. 9 cm

19. How many blocks are needed to build a cube 5 blocks long, 5 blocks wide and 5 blocks high? (1 mark)
   A. 15
   B. 25
   C. 125
   D. 55

20. A cuboid is 7 blocks long, 3 blocks wide and 2 blocks high. What is its volume? (1 mark)
   A. 12 blocks
   B. 21 blocks
   C. 49 blocks
   D. 42 blocks

21. A tank has 50 L of water and 18 L is used. How much is left? (1 mark)
   A. 68 L
   B. 42 L
   C. 22 L
   D. 32 L

22. What is 3 3/4 L + 3 1/2 L? (1 mark)
   A. 7 1/4 L
   B. 7 L
   C. 7 3/4 L
   D. 7 1/2 L

23. What is capacity? (1 mark)
   A. The colour of a container
   B. The amount of liquid a container can hold
   C. The height of a container
   D. The mass of a container

24. A 50 kg sack of rice is packed into bags of 5 kg. How many bags are filled? (1 mark)
   A. 45
   B. 10
   C. 5
   D. 250

25. What is 6 1/4 kg − 2 1/2 kg? (1 mark)
   A. 4 1/4 kg
   B. 3 3/4 kg
   C. 4 kg
   D. 3 1/2 kg

26. Change 17 days to weeks and days. (1 mark)
   A. 2 weeks 3 days
   B. 3 weeks
   C. 3 weeks 2 days
   D. 2 weeks 4 days

27. How long is a lesson that starts at 11:20 a.m. and ends at 1:05 p.m.? (1 mark)
   A. 1 h 45 min
   B. 1 h 30 min
   C. 2 h 45 min
   D. 1 h 55 min

28. Musa has one Ksh 100 note, one Ksh 50 note and two Ksh 20 coins. How much money does he have? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 210
   B. Ksh 150
   C. Ksh 190
   D. Ksh 170

29. How many cents are in Ksh 12? (1 mark)
   A. 112 cents
   B. 1,200 cents
   C. 12,000 cents
   D. 120 cents

30. The table shows the favourite sports of 10 pupils: football 5, netball 3, athletics 1, swimming 1. How many more are there of football than of netball? (1 mark)
   A. 8
   B. 4
   C. 2
   D. 3

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Find the volume of a cuboid that is 6 blocks long, 4 blocks wide and 3 blocks high. Show your working. (3 marks)

32. Add 4,236 and 1,528. Show your working. (3 marks)

33. Ten pupils were asked their favourite fruit and the answers were: mango, banana, mango, orange, banana, mango, pawpaw, mango, banana, orange. (a) Show the data in a tally table. (b) Which fruit is the most popular? (c) How many more pupils chose mango than orange? (5 marks)

34. 38 mangoes are shared equally among 5 children. How many does each child get and how many are left over? (3 marks)

35. Tabitha has 2,450 eggs. She gets 3,875 more. How many eggs does she have now? (3 marks)

36. A store stacks boxes 6 in a row, 3 rows deep and 2 layers high. How many boxes are in the stack? Give one safety rule for stacking. (4 marks)

37. A vendor sells 2 bags of maize (m) and 3 bags of beans (b) on Monday, and 4 bags of maize and 1 bag of beans on Tuesday. (a) Write an expression for Monday. (b) Write an expression for Tuesday. (c) Simplify the expression for the two days together. (5 marks)

38. Subtract 2,718 from 5,432, showing every regrouping step. (4 marks)

39. Write an expression for each: (a) 6 less than k, (b) three times a number b, (c) the cost of 5 pens at p shillings each. (3 marks)

40. Box P is 5 blocks long, 2 wide and 4 high. Box Q is 4 blocks long, 4 wide and 2 high. Which has the greater volume and by how many blocks? (4 marks)

41. Write three reasons why we prepare a shopping list. (3 marks)

42. A school tank held 8,500 litres of water. The school used 3,275 litres in the first week and 1,850 litres in the second week. How much water is left? Check your answer. (5 marks)

43. School starts at 8:00 a.m. and ends at 3:15 p.m. Lunch is from 12:40 p.m. to 1:40 p.m. (a) How long is the school day? (b) How long is it from the start of school to the start of lunch? (c) How long is it from the end of lunch to the end of school? (5 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — MOCK EXAM #5 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24
   Pair up numbers that multiply to 24. The factors are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24.

2. A — 583
   Compare the digits from the left. The largest number is 583.

3. B — 130
   Look at the ones digit 8. It is 5 or more, so go up to the next ten. 128 rounds to 130.

4. D — 210
   Look at the ones digit 5. It is 5 or more, so go up to the next ten. 205 rounds to 210.

5. B — 0
   Check each column from the right for a total of 10 or more, remembering the carried digit. 1,234 + 4,321 needs 0 regroupings.

6. D — add 250
   Each number is 250 more than the one before it, so the rule is add 250.

7. B — 5,850
   2,694 rounds to 2,690 and 3,158 rounds to 3,160. 2,690 + 3,160 = 5,850.

8. C — 7,000
   The rule is subtract 500. 7,500 − 500 = 7,000.

9. A — 4,375
   Subtract from the ones, regrouping when the top digit is smaller. 9,250 − 4,875 = 4,375. Check: 4,375 + 4,875 = 9,250.

10. B — 4,800
   Multiplying by 100 moves each digit two places to the left, so 48 × 100 = 4,800.

11. B — 1/2
   In a proper fraction the numerator is smaller than the denominator, so 1/2 is less than one whole.

12. B — 7/10
   The whole has 10 equal parts and 7 are shaded, so 7/10 is shaded.

13. C — The whole is cut into three parts of the same size
   A fraction shows equal parts of a whole. If the parts are different sizes, one part is not one third.

14. B — 9
   36 ÷ 4 = 9 and 9 × 1 = 9. So 1/4 of 36 is 9.

15. A — 0.9
   Give every number the same number of decimal places and compare from the left. The largest number is 0.9.

16. D — Tens
   The first digit after the decimal point is tenths and the second is hundredths. In 26.91 the digit 2 is in the tens place.

17. A — 3a and 5a
   Like terms have the same letter. 3a and 5a both have the letter a.

18. A — 8 cm
   Subtract the start from the end: 12 − 4 = 8 cm.

19. C — 125
   5 × 5 = 25 per layer and 25 × 5 = 125 blocks.

20. D — 42 blocks
   One layer has 7 × 3 = 21 blocks. There are 2 layers, so the volume is 21 × 2 = 42 blocks.

21. D — 32 L
   50 − 18 = 32 L.

22. A — 7 1/4 L
   Work with the whole litres first and then the parts. 3 3/4 L + 3 1/2 L = 7 1/4 L.

23. B — The amount of liquid a container can hold
   Capacity tells us how much liquid a container holds when it is full.

24. B — 10
   50 ÷ 5 = 10 bags.

25. B — 3 3/4 kg
   Work with the whole kilograms first and then the parts. 6 1/4 kg − 2 1/2 kg = 3 3/4 kg.

26. A — 2 weeks 3 days
   17 ÷ 7 = 2 remainder 3, so 17 days = 2 weeks 3 days.

27. A — 1 h 45 min
   Count on from 11:20 a.m. to 1:05 p.m.. The total is 1 h 45 min.

28. C — Ksh 190
   100 + 50 + 20 + 20 = 190.

29. B — 1,200 cents
   Ksh 1 = 100 cents, so Ksh 12 = 12 × 100 = 1,200 cents.

30. C — 2
   5 − 3 = 2.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: 72 blocks
   Working / marking points: 6 × 4 = 24 blocks in a layer (1 mark); 24 × 3 (1 mark); 72 blocks (1 mark).

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: 5,764
   Working / marking points: Ones 6 + 8 = 14, write 4 carry 1 (1 mark); tens 3 + 2 + 1 = 6 (1 mark); hundreds 2 + 5 = 7, thousands 4 + 1 = 5, answer 5,764 (1 mark).

33. (5 marks)
   Answer: (a) mango 4, banana 3, orange 2, pawpaw 1 (total 10) (b) mango (c) 4 − 2 = 2 pupils
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for a correct table with title and headings, 1 mark for correct tallies and totals, 1 mark for (b), 1 mark for (c).

34. (3 marks)
   Answer: Each child gets 7 mangoes and 3 mangoes are left over.
   Working / marking points: 38 ÷ 5 = 7 remainder 3. 1 mark for the division, 1 mark for 7, 1 mark for 3.

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: 6,325 eggs
   Working / marking points: Ones 0 + 5 = 5; tens 5 + 7 = 12 write 2 carry 1; hundreds 4 + 8 + 1 = 13 write 3 carry 1; thousands 2 + 3 + 1 = 6. 1 mark for method, 1 for regrouping, 1 for answer with unit.

36. (4 marks)
   Answer: 36 boxes. Put heavy boxes at the bottom (or do not stack too high).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 6 × 3 = 18, 1 mark for 18 × 2, 1 mark for 36, 1 mark for a sensible safety rule.

37. (5 marks)
   Answer: (a) 2m + 3b (b) 4m + b (c) 2m + 3b + 4m + b = 6m + 4b
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for (a), 1 mark for (b), 3 marks for (c): 1 mark for adding the expressions, 1 mark for 6m, 1 mark for 4b.

38. (4 marks)
   Answer: 2,714
   Working / marking points: Ones 12 − 8 = 4 (1 mark); tens 2 − 1 = 1 (1 mark); hundreds 14 − 7 = 7 (1 mark); thousands 4 − 2 = 2 (1 mark).

39. (3 marks)
   Answer: (a) k − 6 (b) 3b (c) 5p
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct expression.

40. (4 marks)
   Answer: Box P, by 8 blocks
   Working / marking points: P = 40 (1 mark); Q = 32 (1 mark); P is greater (1 mark); 40 − 32 = 8 (1 mark).

41. (3 marks)
   Answer: To remember everything we need; to buy only what is needed; to avoid spending more than we have.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sensible reason, up to 3 marks.

42. (5 marks)
   Answer: 3,375 litres
   Working / marking points: 8,500 − 3,275 = 5,225 (2 marks); 5,225 − 1,850 = 3,375 (2 marks); check by adding 3,375 + 1,850 + 3,275 = 8,500 (1 mark).

43. (5 marks)
   Answer: (a) 7 hours 15 minutes (b) 4 hours 40 minutes (c) 1 hour 35 minutes
   Working / marking points: (a) 8:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. is 7 hours and then 15 minutes (2 marks); (b) 8:00 to 12:40 is 4 h 40 min (1 mark); (c) 1:40 p.m. to 3:15 p.m. is 1 h 35 min (2 marks).
